mainTopic: A son using his father's נזירות money: the מחלוקת with רבי יוסי and unresolved questions about its details
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: a son may use his dead father's נזירות money because of a special הלכה, not because he inherits it. Then the גמרא asks whether the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי about when a son may do this, and if so, on which case. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי allows it only when the son became a נזיר after his father died. רבי אליעזר, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה answer that 'this is the one' who may use the money, reversing רבי יוסי. Next comes a chain of questions: what if there are two sons, a בכור and a regular son, or money that is הקדש? What if father and son had different kinds of נזירות, or one was טמא and the other טהור? All of these end with תיקו, without an answer. The פרק מי שאמר then closes, and a new פרק opens with בית שמאי's ruling that a mistaken הקדש still counts.

steps.title: It is simply a set rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up the previous discussion: the משנה is teaching a הלכה, a set rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches us that this is a הלכה, a set rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer. A son may use his father's נזירות money because of a fixed הלכה, not because he inherits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the גמרא was asking why only a son and not a daughter may use the father's money. The answer is that this is not about inheritance law at all. It is a received rule that applies to a son only.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (the new point being made)
A set rule received by tradition, here not built on logic or inheritance law

steps.whatToRemember: A son using his father's נזירות money is a special הלכה. It does not come from the laws of inheritance, which is why a daughter cannot do it.

phrases.english: It teaches us that it is a halakha.
phrases.notes: He means a fixed rule from tradition, not something that follows from the son inheriting his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the earlier discussion about why a son, but not a daughter, may use his father's money.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A son's use of his father's נזירות money is a special הלכה, not an inheritance right.

steps.title: Do the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי, and on which case?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: do the רבנן argue with רבי יוסי? If they do, is it about the first case or the second case?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Do the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי or not? And if you say they disagree, is it about the first case (רישא) or the second case (סיפא)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question. It wants to know whether the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי about when a son may use his father's money, and if so, on which part of his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's ruling has two parts. In one case the son may use the money, and in the other case he may not. The question has two layers: first, is there any disagreement at all? Second, if there is, does it concern the רישא, the סיפא, or possibly both?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the learning formula for a real open question)
They disagree
The Sages, the other חכמים
The first clause / the latter clause of a teaching

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Do the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yosei,
or do they not disagree?
And if you say that they disagree,
is it on the first clause or on the latter clause?
phrases.notes: These are the two cases in רבי יוסי's ruling: one where the son may use the money and one where he may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אוֹ לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the previous discussion closed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי at all, and if so, whether it is about the רישא or the סיפא.

steps.title: A ברייתא with רבי יוסי's two cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי יוסי rules that a son who became a נזיר after his father may use the father's money, but if both were נזירים together, the money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: How did the חכמים mean that a man shaves using his father's נזירות? If his father was a נזיר, set aside money for his נזירות, and died, and the son said: 'I am a נזיר on condition that I shave with Father's money,' this is the one who shaves with his father's money. But if both he and his father were נזירים, and the father set aside money for his own נזירות and died, the money goes to נדבה. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer its question by quoting a ברייתא. This step lays out רבי יוסי's two cases, and the next step will show how the other חכמים respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case one (רישא): the father was a נזיר, and after his death the son takes on נזירות on the condition that he can use Father's money. רבי יוסי allows it. Case two (סיפא): father and son were נזירים at the same time. Here רבי יוסי says the money cannot be used by the son and goes to communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Shaves, meaning finishes his נזירות with the shaving and its קרבנות
Set aside money, here for buying his נזירות קרבנות
Shall go to gift offerings, used for voluntary communal קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the first case the son becomes a נזיר only after his father dies. In the second case both were נזירים at the same time. רבי יוסי rules differently on each.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
How did they say
that a man shaves by means of his father's naziriteship?
phrases.notes: He uses the money his father set aside to bring his own end-of-נזירות קרבנות.

phrases.english: One whose father was a nazirite,
and his father set aside money for his naziriteship and died,
and he said: "I am hereby a nazirite

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֲגַלֵּחַ עַל מְעוֹת אַבָּא״
phrases.english: on condition that I shave with Father's money"
this is the one who shaves with his father's money.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁהָיָה הוּא וְאָבִיו נְזִירִים,
phrases.english: But one who was a nazirite together with his father,
and his father set aside money for his naziriteship and died
this money goes to gift offerings,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כֵּיצַד אָמְרוּ הָאִישׁ מְגַלֵּחַ עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer the question of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: Whether, and on which clause, the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that records רבי יוסי's two cases, followed by the other חכמים' response.

steps.title: The other חכמים: 'This is the one who shaves'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה respond: 'This is the one who shaves with his father's money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה said: This is the one who shaves with his father's money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the other חכמים' view. This is the part the גמרא will use to answer its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their words 'זה הוא' point to the second case, where father and son were נזירים together. They say this is exactly the case where the son may use the money. That is the opposite of רבי יוסי's ruling, so their wording suggests they disagree with him on both the רישא and the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the one, an emphatic phrase that points to a specific case
His father's money set aside for נזירות קרבנות

steps.whyThisMatters: The strong wording 'זה הוא' answers the question of step 2. It shows the רבנן reverse רבי יוסי completely, disagreeing on both clauses.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הוּא שֶׁמְּגַלֵּחַ עַל מְעוֹת אָבִיו.
phrases.english: This is the one who shaves with his father's money.
phrases.notes: 'This' points to the case רבי יוסי just ruled out, where father and son were both נזירים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמְרוּ: זֶה הוּא שֶׁמְּגַלֵּחַ עַל מְעוֹת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 3 with the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי on both clauses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The emphatic wording 'זה הוא שמגלח על מעות אביו' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Two sons who are both נזירים
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks what happens if a father with נזירות money has two sons who are נזירים. Does whoever shaves first get it all, or do they split it like an inheritance?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: If a man has two sons who are נזירים, what is the law? Do we know this rule as a special הלכה, so whoever shaves first has shaved (and uses all the money)? Or perhaps we know it from the laws of inheritance, so each son gets half?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks a new question about the rule that a son may shave with his father's money: what if there are two sons who are נזירים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question depends on where the rule comes from. If it is a special הלכה that has nothing to do with inheritance, the money goes to whichever son uses it first. If it works like ירושה, the two brothers split it evenly.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, he raised a question (an open problem, a בעיא)
We learned it as a fixed הלכה (a received rule, not from logic)
Inheritance
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the question)
Half

steps.whyThisMatters: The question 'special הלכה or ירושה?' is the key that drives the next questions too.

phrases.english: Rabba asked:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי בָנִים נְזִירִים, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If he has two sons who are nazirites, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the father who left money for his own נזירות, from the ברייתא in step 3.

phrases.english: Do we learn it as a set halacha:
whoever shaves first has shaved (and uses the money),
or perhaps we learn it from inheritance,
and it is half (for each)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ruling from the ברייתא and tests how it applies when there are two sons.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the son's right to the father's money a special הלכה (first come, first served) or a kind of inheritance (split equally)?

steps.title: A firstborn and a regular son
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a בכור and a regular son. If this works like ירושה, does the בכור get a double share of the money for his shaving?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: What if the sons are a firstborn and a regular son? If we know this as a special הלכה, then a son does not need to shave based on the share he inherits. Or perhaps it is inheritance, and just as the firstborn takes a double portion, so too he shaves with a double portion?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a similar question using the same two sides, this time with a בכור and a regular son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושה, a בכור gets a double share (פי שנים). If this money counts as ירושה, the בכור should get double. If it is a special הלכה, inheritance shares do not matter here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son
A regular son (not the firstborn)
A double portion (the בכור's share in ירושה)
According to what he takes (his share)

phrases.english: Rava asked:
A firstborn and a regular son, what is the law?
Do we learn it as a set halacha,
and therefore he does not need to shave
according to what he takes (as his share).
Or perhaps it is inheritance,
and just as he (the firstborn) takes a double portion,
so too he shaves (with a double portion)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'הלכה or ירושה' split as רבה's question, applied to a בכור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a בכור get a double share of the father's נזירות money, the way he does in ירושה?

steps.title: Even if it is inheritance: does the double share apply to הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: Even if we say it is ירושה, maybe the בכור's double share applies only to ordinary property (חולין), not to money meant for קרבנות (הקדש).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is inheritance, and he shaves according to what he takes, maybe the firstborn's double portion applies only to non-holy property, but not to holy property? Or perhaps, since he acquires the money for his shaving, there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a further question on top of רבא's: even if this money is ירושה, does the בכור's double share apply to money set aside for holy use?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double share of a בכור might be limited to חולין, ordinary property. Money set aside for a נזיר's קרבנות is הקדש. On the other side, since the son really does acquire the money for his own shaving, maybe it is treated like any other inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (we accept one side of the question and ask a new one from there)
Ordinary, non-holy property
Holy, consecrated property
There is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not settle רבא's question. It only says: even if we decided it is ירושה, a new doubt comes up.

phrases.english: And if you say:
it is inheritance, and he shaves according to what he takes,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחוּלִּין הוּא דְּאִית לֵיהּ פִּי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: (still,) it is with non-holy property that he has a double portion,
but with holy property, no.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּקָנֵי לֵיהּ לְגִלּוּחַ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since he acquires it for shaving,
there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the ירושה side of step 6 and asks whether the בכור's double share applies to הקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the בכור's double portion apply to consecrated money set aside for a נזיר's קרבנות, or only to חולין?

steps.title: Father and son with different kinds of נזירות
steps.stepSummary: What if one of them is a נזיר עולם and the other a regular נזיר? Does the rule apply only when both are regular נזירים?
steps.simpleTranslation: If his father was a permanent נזיר and he is a regular נזיר, or his father was a regular נזיר and he is a permanent נזיר, what is the law? When we learned the הלכה, was it only for regular נזירות, or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks one more open question: can the son use his father's money if the two of them have different kinds of נזירות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר עולם and a נזיר סתם have different rules and different times for bringing קרבנות. Maybe the rule was only given for the normal case, where both are regular נזירים. Or maybe the rule covers any son who is a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent נזיר, a נזיר forever
A regular נזיר with no time stated (thirty days)
What (is the law)?

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו נְזִיר עוֹלָם וְהוּא נָזִיר סְתָם,
phrases.english: His father is a permanent nazirite and he is a regular nazirite,
phrases.notes: A נזיר עולם is a נזיר for life who lightens his hair from time to time and brings קרבנות each time, unlike a regular נזיר whose term simply ends.

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו נָזִיר סְתָם וְהוּא נְזִיר עוֹלָם, מַאי?
phrases.english: his father is a regular nazirite and he is a permanent nazirite, what is the law?
When we learned the halacha, was it about regular nazirite vows,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבִיו נְזִיר עוֹלָם וְהוּא נָזִיר סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another test of the same ruling from the ברייתא, now about mixed kinds of נזירות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule that a son shaves with his father's money apply only when both are a נזיר סתם, or also when one is a נזיר עולם?

steps.title: רב אשי asks about a pure father and impure son, or the reverse
steps.stepSummary: Even if a נזיר עולם and a regular נזיר can share, since both are pure נזירות, רב אשי asks what happens if one was a טמא נזיר and the other a טהור נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here both cases are pure נזירות, so the son can use the money, רב אשי asks: what if his father was an impure נזיר and he is a pure נזיר? Or his father was a pure נזיר and he is an impure נזיר? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that the previous question might be answered with 'yes, it works', and then רב אשי asks a harder version of it. Now the difference between father and son is about purity, not about the type of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last question, both the נזיר עולם and the regular נזיר still had a pure נזירות, so they are similar enough. A טמא נזיר brings different קרבנות from a טהור נזיר, so the gap here is bigger. רב אשי asks whether money set aside for one kind of shaving can pay for the other kind.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (if you answer the last question this way). It opens a harder follow-up question.
This one and that one, meaning both cases
A נזירות kept in purity, which ends with the regular shaving and קרבנות
A נזיר who became impure and must shave and bring the קרבנות of impurity
Asks a question he wants resolved

steps.confusionAlert: 'אם תימצי לומר' does not mean the גמרא has decided the earlier question. It only means: even if you answer it this way, here is a harder case.

phrases.english: And if you say:
phrases.notes: He means: even if you answer the last question (נזיר עולם and regular נזיר) by saying it works.

phrases.english: here, both this one and that one
are ritually pure naziriteship,
Rav Ashi asks:
His father was an impure nazirite,
and he is a pure nazirite.
His father was a pure nazirite,
and he is an impure nazirite: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר הָכָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי נְזִירוּת טׇהֳרָה בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8's question with a bigger difference: purity versus impurity instead of a lifelong versus a regular נזירות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a son who is a טהור נזיר use money left for his father's טמא נזירות, or the reverse?

steps.title: The questions are left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stands without an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not find an answer to these questions, so it leaves them open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. It closes the whole chain of questions from רבה, רבא and רב אשי about splitting the father's נזירות money.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: The son may shave with his father's leftover נזירות money, but the details are left open: two sons, a בכור, a נזיר עולם, and a טמא versus טהור נזיר.

phrases.english: Let it stand.
phrases.notes: This one word closes all the questions from רבה, רבא and רב אשי: none of them gets an answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes step 9 and the earlier questions without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about how the father's נזירות money works in these special cases remain unresolved.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter מי שאמר
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for the פרק called מי שאמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter מי שאמר.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said when a פרק is finished. It shows we hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. Said at the end of a פרק.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One who said"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally ends the פרק after the תיקו.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק מי שאמר is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: בית שמאי say a mistaken consecration still counts
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה: בית שמאי rule that הקדש made by mistake is still הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: consecration made in error is consecration.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. בית שמאי state that if someone makes something הקדש because of a mistake, it still becomes הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we might think a vow made by mistake does not count. בית שמאי hold that a mistaken הקדש still takes effect. This sets up the topic of the new פרק, which will look at mistaken vows, including נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Making something holy, given to the בית המקדש
A consecration made because of a mistake
The school of שמאי, the students of שמאי

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
consecration made in error is consecration,

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים הֶקְדֵּשׁ טָעוּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק, not connected to the earlier argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, הקדש made by mistake still takes effect.
